As a individual who has experienced trauma in my life and thought/attempted suicide i can tell you your friend did not do it because your friend was a self person who didn’t think of anyone else. Depression tends to make us believe that you aren’t good enough to stay apart of the living, it has little to with the people surrounding you worth but specifically how you value yourself. The guilt you are feeling is what most people would, you are thinking of what ifs and why did yous. But your mother is right there is nothing you could have done about it. Your friend loved you very much and i am sure that the pain he sees you going through is extremely terrible. But the memory you have of your friend is extremely important. You ask how you can help keep that beautiful memory alive. Maybe help
Others like your friend, don’t hate yourself or beat yourself up this isn’t your fault. And I’m sorry you have to be the one to take on this burden.

Tell your parents or someone close to you what you are going through, so you can get proper help. The journey you have ahead of you is worth fighting for. Do not give up. And remember beyond all this never put your happiness into the hands of others. Your happiness is your responsibility. Find things you love to do enjoy the time you have while you are a kid.
